launches.line: Greenhouse launched Greenhouse in Claude, an open beta plugin for Greenhouse Recruiting customers on Core, Plus and Pro plans that gives a daily brief, candidate status, pipeline review, debrief prep and draft scorecards inside Claude, and can advance candidates, schedule interviews and create jobs within each user's existing permissions.
launches.quote: Greenhouse remains the system of record, and teams can ask questions and take action from Claude.
launches.materiality: MATERIAL, saved. Tier A, net-new product with write actions, in a tool this reader already uses (recent featured items on Claude for TA). Missed by the 4 Nov sweep, not in the featured log, inside the 8 week window. Caveats: open beta, not GA; dated 22 Oct so it is 3.5 weeks old; it is built on MCP, so a strict reader of the 'no integrations' rule could call it an integration. My call: it is a product with its own skills and actions, not a data sync.

ai_news.title: AI-assisted deception in job applications: four in ten recruiters have detected or suspect its use
ai_news.source: The Stepstone Group (press release, Hiring Trends Update, via EQS News)
ai_news.second_source_note: The German-language release as carried by onvista; all figures, sample and fieldwork dates match. It is the same issuer's release, not independent reporting: no independent journalism found on the day. Not regulatory or legal.
ai_news.why_it_matters: Candidate fraud and AI-written applications are a live worry for in-house and agency recruiters. This gives quotable, freshly dated numbers from a large recruiter sample (1,227) on how often it is happening and what form it takes, including prompt injections aimed at AI screening and deepfakes in video interviews. Clearly labelled as Germany and as a vendor survey. Nothing regulatory, legal or model-related this week cleared the bar for this reader.

points.claim: Share of recruiters in Germany who identified or suspected AI-assisted deception in the past twelve months
points.quote: Four in ten recruiters (41%) in Germany have identified or suspected cases of AI-assisted deception
73% of recruiters say they have become more sceptical when assessing job applications

points.claim: Prompt injections in application documents (base: 505 recruiters reporting identified or suspected cases)
points.quote: 26% have encountered hidden instructions embedded in application documents

points.claim: Someone other than the applicant attended the interview (same base)
points.quote: over one in five (22%) report cases where someone other than the applicant attended the interview
A further 8% have even encountered deepfakes in video interviews

points.claim: Candidates who would not apply if AI made the final hiring decision
points.quote: 61% would not apply for a job if AI made the final hiring decision

points.figure: 7,652 candidates and 1,227 recruiters in Germany, fieldwork 24 September to 13 October 2026

ai_news_runner_up.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
